criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Look v2 is carried. Every frame is saturated violet, rose and kraft with no near-black room, and most subjects fill half the frame. S5 is the best frame: two kraft-wrapped ream stacks on an oak table, the 2032 stack about 2.2x the 2027 one (machine_qa S5 measured ratio 2.2013 against a truth of 2.2013, err 0), a steel rule and a raking dusk window. A reader gets the growth without reading a number. S9 also works: the 2032 stack with the envelope and the gold line, a pen and the window cast on the wall. S6 has a real chamber with the US and Texas flags, a seal and cast flag shadows, and the two local piles read as about 1 ream against 2. Where it falls short: S7, the deck's planned showstopper, is the weakest frame. The blurred stack reads as a striped smear on a flat crimson-and-plum gradient, and the shadow runs diagonally down-left without clearly crossing the gold highlighted line, which is the frame's whole idea. S3's rubber mat has stripe moire and broken glyph-like specks around the stray Register page at the bottom, which also crowds the footer. On S4 the top 40 percent is a flat textured purple field holding the type, and the relief sits under it like a plate. On the cover the 1,947-sheet stack at the rack's foot is tiny and says nothing at feed size.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The spine holds across the contact sheet: one violet, rose and kraft palette, the serif hook with the Manrope dek, the mono counter and claim line, and dusk gold kept to the proposal's words (S1 clipped page, S4 paragraph, S7 line, S9 letter). The paper motif changes state and does real work: page and small stack (1), page relief (4), the two stacks (5), local piles (6), page under the stack (7), letter on the 2032 stack (9). The 2032 stack returns on 5, 7 and 9 as a recurring object. S8's enamel sorter on a studio sweep and S3's hall sit slightly outside the paper world, but the storyboard declares both as grafts.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every slide numeral traces to the claims file: $1,947,310,000 (c26), $4,286,040,000 (c31), $507,450,000 (c32), $1,116,890,000 (c37), 1987 (c7), November 18th (c2), November 20th (c45), 30 days (c41), December 20th (c43). '$4.3 billion' is a rounding of c31, and the Tribune's c14 agrees. The S7 quote is verbatim from c38. The money figures are primary: the fiscal note in the Texas Register. Two looser points. The caption's Eckhardt handover (c15, c17) rests on Tribune paraphrase. 'Comments must arrive by December 20th' on S9 is date math (November 20th plus 30 days), so I am assuming it sits in figures.json. The cover headline 'Texas may stop taxing AI as data processing' assumes AI is taxed as data processing today, which Huffines disputes (c8). The fiscal note's revenue loss supports the reading, but the phrasing leans one way.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan swiping once learns who decided (Comptroller Don Huffines), what (proposed Rule 3.308 amendments counting cloud, AI and quantum as untaxed hosted technology services), the cost by the office's own note (state and local, 2027 and 2032), that it is not adopted, and how to act: Robin Robinson, the email address on S9 and December 20th. That is near the 10. Two things keep it off. First, no slide says who pays this tax today or what changes for a Texas business's or a city's budget, so the local loss on S6 stays general ('Cities, counties and transit lose too' names no place). Second, the stake that most decides whether a comment matters is only in the caption: Eckhardt takes office January 1st and asked him to halt rule changes begun since August 1st (c15, c17, and c18 for his refusal).

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover earns the swipe. S2 pays at once with the 1987 definition, and the turn lands at S5 to S7: the loss grows, locals lose, and then the same note calls the effect 'insignificant'. The close is an action. Some slides overlap. S3 and S4 are both definitional beats a reader could take as one. S8 and S9 both carry December 20th, and S8's 'Thirty days' mechanics could fold into S9 without loss.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and on register, with no doom and no boosterism. S7's dek states the contradiction plainly without sarcasm, which is the right call. It is also bureaucratic in places and has almost no Texas texture. S3's 'A customer using a provider's software, platform or computing resources on its own data would not be a data processing service' is the rule's language more than a person's. No slide grounds the stake in a Texas place, business or budget.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: From the topics ledger, the last six decks (nos. 83 to 88) were university or federal research and program stories. This is a state-tax rulemaking deck in the watch tone, built on paper and money stacks: a new structure and a new opening move. The familiar move is the gold accent meaning one thing, which no. 88 also ran as 'dusk gold' the day before, and nos. 82, 86 and 87 also gave gold a single meaning. No comptroller or data processing tax topic appears inside the 30-day window.

named_defects: S7: the showstopper's shadow does not visibly cross the gold highlighted line, and the blurred stack reads as a striped smear on a flat gradient
S3: stripe moire and broken specks on the floor mat, and the stray Register page crowds the footer at bottom centre
S5: neither stack is labelled by year, so the reader infers 2027 left and 2032 right from the dek
S4: the top 40 percent is a flat purple field holding the type over the relief
S1: the fiscal 2027 ream stack is too small to read as the estimate at feed size
Eckhardt's January 1st takeover and halt request (c15, c17) are in the caption only, and that is the stake deciding whether a comment matters
S8 and S9 duplicate the December 20th deadline
machine_qa warns that S7's hook and dek sit outside the 80 px safe zone on the right (warn, not fail)
final/thumbs/slide-01.png does not exist. Feed size was judged from final/contact_sheet.png
one_sentence_fix: Replace S8's duplicate deadline frame with the handover beat from c15, c17 and c18: Eckhardt takes office January 1st, has asked Huffines to halt rule changes begun since August 1st, and he says he will keep making rules until he leaves. Fold the 30-day comment mechanics into S9 so the reader sees on the slides why a comment by December 20th matters.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The planned showstopper fails its own idea. The out-of-focus stack is a striped smear against a flat crimson-and-plum gradient, and its shadow falls diagonally away from the gold line instead of across it.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Lower the coral key to graze from behind the stack along the page's long axis so the stack's shadow lands squarely across the gold line. Pull focus slightly so the torn top ream and the kraft wrappers read, and give the back wall a lit surface instead of a gradient.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The perforated floor mat aliases into stripe moire with broken glyph-like specks, and the stray Register page at the bottom clips into the footer band.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Swap the mat's striped texture for a low-frequency rubber or graphite tile with mipmapped anisotropic filtering. Move the Register page up and left onto clean floor above the footer, or cut it.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The relief starts 40 percent down, leaving a flat textured purple field as a type plate above it.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Raise the camera and enlarge the Register page so the oak blotter and page run to the top edge. Seat the type on the blotter's dark lower-left margin, letting the relief own the frame.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The fiscal 2027 ream stack, the cover's link to the estimate, is a small kraft block at the rack's foot that reads as nothing at feed size.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Bring the camera down and forward so the stack sits in the foreground at one depth with the rack, still drawn to its measured height, and its contact shadow and torn wrapper are visible.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The stacks carry no year, so the frame's strongest comparison depends on reading the dek.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Add a small accent-pill label at each stack's base, FY2027 and FY2032. The years are already claim-backed numerals.
